# At GOAMD64=v3 only the AVX2 check is omitted: the 8 and 16-bit
# slice sums keep their AVX512 guard. At v4 both checks are omitted
# while the masked tail loads stay. The v3 AVX2 omission and the
# scalar path live in logos_simd_feature_gate.txt and
# logos_simd_gate_branch.txt; this script pins the AVX512 level.
[!GOARCH:amd64] skip 'gate objdump needs amd64'
[!GOOS:linux] skip 'host cpu probe reads /proc/cpuinfo'

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env GOEXPERIMENT=simd

cd m
env GOAMD64=v3
logos build -o $WORK/exe3 .
go tool objdump -s '^main\.sumU8$' $WORK/exe3
stdout 'VMOVDQU8\.Z'
stdout 'AVX512'
go tool objdump -s '^main\.sumI16$' $WORK/exe3
stdout 'VMOVDQU16\.Z'
stdout 'AVX512'
env GOAMD64=v1
exec go run ./runmin v3 $WORK/exe3
stdout '^(sums ok|host below v3)$'

env GOAMD64=v4
logos build -o $WORK/exe4 .
go tool objdump -s '^main\.sumU8$' $WORK/exe4
stdout 'VMOVDQU8\.Z'
! stdout 'AVX512'
go tool objdump -s '^main\.sumI16$' $WORK/exe4
stdout 'VMOVDQU16\.Z'
! stdout 'AVX512'
env GOAMD64=v1
exec go run ./runmin v4 $WORK/exe4
stdout '^(sums ok|host below v4)$'

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/gateavx512

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

//go:noinline
func sumU8(xs []uint8) uint8 { return xs.sum() }

//go:noinline
func sumI16(xs []int16) int16 { return xs.sum() }

func oracleU8(xs []uint8) uint8 {
	t := uint8(0)
	for _, v := range xs {
		t += v
	}
	return t
}

func oracleI16(xs []int16) int16 {
	t := int16(0)
	for _, v := range xs {
		t += v
	}
	return t
}

func main() {
	us := make([]uint8, 70)
	ss := make([]int16, 70)
	for i := range us {
		us[i] = uint8(i * 3)
		ss[i] = int16(i*7 - 100)
	}
	if sumU8(us) != oracleU8(us) {
		panic("u8 sum mismatch")
	}
	if sumI16(ss) != oracleI16(ss) {
		panic("i16 sum mismatch")
	}
	fmt.Println("sums ok")
}

-- m/runmin/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
)

// runmin execs the binary named by its second argument only when the
// host CPU meets the GOAMD64 level given as the first argument (v1
// through v4); otherwise it prints "host below <level>" and exits 0.
// The cpuinfo probe is Linux-only: the script header skips elsewhere.
var levelFlags = map[byte][]string{
	'2': {"cx16", "lahf_lm", "popcnt", "sse3", "sse4_1", "sse4_2", "ssse3"},
	'3': {"avx", "avx2", "bmi1", "bmi2", "f16c", "fma", "lzcnt", "movbe", "osxsave"},
	'4': {"avx512f", "avx512bw", "avx512cd", "avx512dq", "avx512vl"},
}

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 3 || len(os.Args[1]) != 2 || os.Args[1][0] != 'v' {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: runmin v<level> <binary>")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/cpuinfo")
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "read cpuinfo:", err)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	set := map[string]bool{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "flags") {
			continue
		}
		parts := strings.SplitN(line, ":", 2)
		if len(parts) != 2 {
			continue
		}
		for _, f := range strings.Fields(parts[1]) {
			set[f] = true
		}
		break
	}
	for lvl := byte('2'); lvl <= os.Args[1][1]; lvl++ {
		for _, f := range levelFlags[lvl] {
			if !set[f] {
				fmt.Println("host below " + os.Args[1])
				return
			}
		}
	}
	cmd := exec.Command(os.Args[2])
	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "runmin:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
